subject.title: Feature Request: Plugin Circuit Breaker for graceful degradation

question: Should OpenClaw add a generic plugin-runtime circuit breaker, keep breaker behavior plugin-local, or land telemetry-only plugin attribution first?
rationale: The remaining work crosses plugin SDK/runtime behavior, persisted state, operator controls, default fail modes, and compatibility for existing external plugins, so automation cannot safely choose the product contract.

options.title: Design a generic breaker
options.body: Create a framework-level breaker with explicit hook/plugin attribution, passive rollout defaults, operator status/reset surfaces, and compatibility tests before enforcing skips.

options.title: Keep breakers plugin-local
options.body: Close the core feature direction and ask high-risk plugins to own their own breaker behavior through plugin-local configuration and docs.

options.title: Land telemetry first
options.body: Add only plugin failure attribution and health reporting now, then revisit automatic degradation after maintainers see real failure data.

recommendation.title: Design a generic breaker
recommendation.body: Create a framework-level breaker with explicit hook/plugin attribution, passive rollout defaults, operator status/reset surfaces, and compatibility tests before enforcing skips.

likelyOwner.reason: This owner has the strongest recent history on the plugin hook runner and adjacent quarantine/breaker surfaces that would define the core contract.
